title: Physics-Inspired Visual AI
subtitle: Grounding Foundation, Generative, and World Models in Physical Principles
overview: Visual AI is entering an era of powerful foundation, generative, and world models. Yet visual plausibility alone does not guarantee physical validity. This special issue explores how the structure of the physical world can ground what models perceive, generate, and predict.
scope: We invite research that connects geometry, illumination, reflectance, materials, optics, sensors, and dynamics with large-scale visual learning. In the complementary direction, learned representations and generative priors can advance inverse problems, reconstruction, rendering, restoration, and computational imaging.

topics.title: Physics-grounded foundation models
topics.description: Physical priors for visual and vision-language foundation models; geometric and photometric reasoning; robust representations grounded in image formation.

topics.title: Physics-consistent generative models
topics.description: Physically valid image, video, and 3D generation; controllable illumination and materials; generative priors for inverse rendering and reconstruction.

topics.title: Physics-aware world models & embodied AI
topics.description: Learning and predicting physical dynamics; consistent scene representations; perception and simulation that support interaction with the physical world.

topics.title: Physics-constrained data & sensors
topics.description: Sensor-aware learning and acquisition; computational imaging; physically grounded synthetic data; multimodal sensing and measurement consistency.

topics.title: Evaluation, benchmarks & applications
topics.description: Measuring physical validity beyond perceptual quality; diagnostic benchmarks, reproducible evaluation, and applications that test robustness and generalization.
